description:
Spatial convergence of the UPWIND-BIASED, MONOTONE conservative flux-form ZONAL advection operator grids/latlon3d/rules/ppm_flux_D_lon_mono_periodic, driven by problems/latlon3d_advection_zonal_ppm_flux_mono. 

THE ORDER IS SET BY THE LIMITER, AND IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The eq (1.10) limiter cannot distinguish a smooth extremum from an oscillation, and q*(lambda) = 2 + sin(lambda) has TWO smooth extrema on the circle, so the limiter fires at both on every mesh however fine and clips the parabola there. This is the textbook SECOND-ORDER-AT-SMOOTH-EXTREMA behaviour of the CW84 limiter, and it is what the ladder measures: median pairwise rate L2 1.88 (pairwise 1.78 / 1.88 / 1.90) and Linf 1.94 (1.79 / 1.94 / 1.98), both climbing toward 2 from below. expected_order 1.91 is the MEASURED value -- the midpoint of the two norms' medians, not a nominal one -- and order_tolerance 0.30 is the same convention the vertical monotone sibling (latlon3d_advection_vertical_ppm_flux_mono, expected_order 2.24 +/- 0.30) uses, wide enough to span both norms and the residual pre-asymptotic drift in the rates. The UNLIMITED sibling case latlon3d_advection_zonal_ppm_flux measures clean fourth order (3.99 / 3.99) on the IDENTICAL MMS, which localises this entire shortfall to the limiter and to nothing else. That is the deliberate trade: formal order you cannot realize on a real tracer field, exchanged for the boundedness you always need. Colella-Sekora (2008) is the documented follow-on that would recover it. 

FORCED-STEADY (TRUNCATION) IDIOM, on a MMS that is BIT-FOR-BIT the donor-cell driver's. q*(lambda) = 2 + sin(lambda) is an exact steady state of the forced equation (the state is seeded with its exact CELL MEAN, and src is the exact flux divergence -- for a finite-volume cell simply the difference of the exact face fluxes times the exact spherical weight), so the drift measured at t = 0.1 IS the operator's truncation error and the observed rate is the truncation order. Because latlon3d_advection_zonal_upwind_flux, latlon3d_advection_zonal_ppm_flux and latlon3d_advection_zonal_ppm_flux_mono differ ONLY in the rule they import, the three measured orders are directly comparable and every difference between them is a property of the OPERATOR alone. 

THE SWEEP REFINES NLON ONLY, AND THAT IS THE POINT. NLAT = 5 and NLEV = 4 are pinned at the problem's rule-import edge. The polar metric weights are therefore EXERCISED but not REFINED: at NLAT = 5 the half-polar cap rows carry dphi_lat/dS_lat ~ 5.2 against ~1.0 in the tropics, so the cap rows dominate the Linf norm at every rung -- but because dphi never shrinks, the lat-lon coordinate singularity that stalls the MERIDIONAL operator's pointwise Linf under refinement cannot contaminate the zonal order. What is left is a clean zonal check. The ladder starts at 32 (the same rung the donor-cell zonal sweep starts at), well clear of the NLON >= 7 the seven-column monotone tiling needs. 

WHAT THIS GUARDS. The wind U = U0 (0.5 + cos lambda) a(j) b(k) is a declared THREE-DIMENSIONAL face-staggered field on the lon_nodes axis that CHANGES SIGN (westward on the 120-degree arc around lambda = 180), so both branches of the upwind donor selection fire in every row, and the a(j) b(k) modulation means a stencil that mis-indexed U as a column profile would be caught rather than silently agreeing. The rule enforces the periodic wrap ITSELF (cell NLON's east face reuses U[1], never U[NLON+1]), which makes sum_i D exactly 0.0; that is verified out-of-band rather than here, because this manifest measures ORDER, not conservation. 

INTEGRATOR CONFIG REPAIR (2026-07-23) -- GOLDEN RESET, NOT A REFRESH. This manifest used to pin its solver under a SINGULAR top-level "integrator" key. NO runner reads that key: run-julia.jl reads integrators.julia, run-python.py integrators.python and run-rust.sh integrators.rust, each falling back to its OWN default when its per-binding block is absent. The pinned reltol 1e-11 / abstol 1e-13 therefore never took effect and every committed golden here was in fact produced at the Julia runner's default Tsit5 reltol 1e-10 / abstol 1e-12. That was verified rather than assumed: re-running the sweep with the block deliberately set back to 1e-10 / 1e-12 reproduces the pre-repair golden to the last bit. The key is now spelled integrators.julia, so the documented tolerances bind, and the goldens are regenerated at them through scripts/regenerate-goldens.sh. The golden values consequently MOVE -- that is the tolerance change becoming real, a behavioural correction and not a refresh-to-green. The observed orders are unaffected (the pairwise rates quoted above are the post-repair ones and are unchanged to the precision quoted, except where this manifest says otherwise), because a tolerance that was already far below the spatial truncation error at every retained rung moves only the digits it reaches. The same commit adds the integrators.python block and puts python in bindings_required: the Python binding was never scope-excluded here, and compare-outputs.py gates any binding that produces a record regardless of bindings_required, so python was eligible all along and is now declared and measured rather than left implicit. 

PYTHON COST (measured 2026-07-23, and ACCEPTED rather than capped). This is the most expensive Python case in the flux family by a wide margin: the full 32/64/128/256 ladder took ~38 min wall on one core (LSODA rtol 1e-12 / atol 1e-14, loaded shared host) against ~1.5 min for the UNLIMITED sibling's ladder. The cause is the operator, not the tolerance -- the eq. (1.8) / eq. (1.10) limiter pair puts min/max branches in the RHS, so the right-hand side is only piecewise smooth and LSODA pays for it in step count and repeated Jacobian/stiffness reassessment. A reduced Python-only ladder is NOT available as a remedy: scripts/compare-outputs.py gates a binding's resolution set against the GOLDEN's set and fails on any mismatch, so the ladder is shared by construction, and shortening it would weaken the order claim for EVERY binding rather than just cheapen this one. The only per-binding cap the harness does offer is scope_excluded, which is all-or-nothing and would drop exactly the case where a second, independently written limiter is most worth cross-checking. So the cost is paid deliberately. It is also the number to budget against before adding any further monotone rung: the last rung alone is the majority of the total.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
